groups.title: set-config.js: support writing multiple config.yml levers in one invocation
groups.body:
Filed by wrap-up reflect (light mode, record #1971's run, refs #1971).

## Current State

`bin/set-config.js` writes exactly one `config.yml` lever per invocation (`--key <lever> --value
<value>`). The documented recovery path for an inherited run directory that reached `/flow`'s Step
3 with no `config.yml` yet (`flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s "Adopting an inherited run directory", case
3) requires computing and writing all 13 canonical Manifesto levers before the pipeline can
proceed. Record #1971's own wrap-up run hit exactly that case and needed 13 sequential
`set-config.js` invocations to backfill the Manifesto.

Evidence: run `2026-09-08T115203-record-1971`'s own Step 3 recovery — 13 separate
`node bin/set-config.js --run ... --key ... --value ...` Bash calls to write `mode`,
`scope-creep`, `overlap`, `design-intent`, `leftover-default`, `auto-fix-threshold`,
`review-auto-apply-ceiling`, `tidy-aggressiveness`, `ceremony-profile`, `model-stance`,
`merge-verification`, `design-critique`, `merge-authorization`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `bin/set-config.js` accepts a batch form (e.g. repeated `--key X --value Y` pairs, or a
      `--from-json <file>` of `{lever: value}` pairs) that validates and writes every pair in one
      invocation, using the same per-lever validation (`validateLever`) it already runs today.
- [ ] The single-pair form (`--key <lever> --value <value>`) keeps working unchanged — this is
      additive, not a breaking CLI change.
- [ ] `flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s case 3 recovery procedure references the batch form once it
      exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A caller can write all 13 canonical Manifesto levers via one `set-config.js` invocation instead
  of 13.
- Existing single-key callers (the Ceremony escape hatch, `flow/manifesto.md`'s per-lever writes)
  are unaffected.

groups.title: pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md Steps 4 and 6 describe verify calls only in prose, with no literal invocation or conformance test
groups.body:
## Current State
`plugin/skills/pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md` Step 4 (line 71) already cites its verify function with a full call signature in prose — "`bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-claim-race.js`'s `verifyClaimRaceOutcome(attemptRunIds, liveClaim, inProgressLabelCount)` is this verdict's mechanical reference implementation" — matching the established sibling pattern (`composeFixesBlock`, `crossReferenceKeyFiles`), which also cite function name in descriptive prose rather than a literal executable `node -e` shell block (confirmed: neither sibling actually has a literal `node -e` invocation in its skill file either — `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s `composeFixesBlock` citation and `record-creation-subissues.md`'s `crossReferenceKeyFiles(units, grep)` citation are both prose name+signature mentions). Step 6 (line 89), however, cites `verifyCleanupTable`/`renderCleanupTable` by name only, without the call-signature parens Step 4 uses. Neither citation is pinned by a prose-conformance test the way the siblings are: `tests/bundle-fixes-reconciliation-2015.test.js` pins `composeFixesBlock`'s citation (`assert.match(section, /composeFixesBlock/)`), and `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js` pins `crossReferenceKeyFiles(units, grep)`'s citation and separately asserts the cited module actually exports it. Nothing pins Steps 4/6's citations here, so a rename or removal of either function reference would go undetected.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add the full call signature to Step 6's `verifyCleanupTable` citation, matching Step 4's style: `verifyCleanupTable(rows)` (and `renderCleanupTable(rows)`, both exported from `bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js`).
- [ ] Add a prose-conformance test (new file, e.g. `tests/pipeline-smoke-test-verify-prose.test.js`) mirroring `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js`'s pattern: assert Step 4 cites `verifyClaimRaceOutcome(attemptRunIds, liveClaim, inProgressLabelCount)`, assert Step 6 cites `verifyCleanupTable(rows)`, and assert both cited modules actually export those functions (`require('../plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-claim-race')`/`verify-cleanup`).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md` Steps 4 and 6 each cite their verify function with its full call signature in prose (matching the sibling `composeFixesBlock`/`crossReferenceKeyFiles` citation style — a named prose citation, not a literal `node -e` shell block, since neither sibling uses one either).
2. A new prose-conformance test fails if either citation string is removed, or if the cited function is renamed/no longer exported by its module.

## Technical Approach
The raw finding's framing ("siblings have a literal `node -e` invocation snippet") doesn't hold on inspection — neither `composeFixesBlock` nor `crossReferenceKeyFiles` has one; both use a prose name+signature citation pinned by a conformance test. The real gap here is narrower: Step 6's citation is missing its call-signature parens (Step 4's already has them), and neither Step 4 nor Step 6's citation is test-pinned at all. Mirror `specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js`'s two-part pattern (citation-string match + module-export assertion) rather than inventing a new test shape.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md` — Step 4 citation (line 71, already has the right shape), Step 6 citation (line 89, needs the signature added)
- `plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-claim-race.js` — exports `verifyClaimRaceOutcome`
- `plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js` — exports `verifyCleanupTable`, `renderCleanupTable`
- `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js` — the pattern to mirror for the new test

groups.title: verify-cleanup.js's renderCleanupTable doesn't escape pipe characters, unlike engine-verify.js's sanitizeCell
groups.body:
## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js`'s `renderCleanupTable` (line 40) interpolates `row.artifact` directly into a markdown table row with no pipe-character escaping: `` `| ${row.artifact} | ${row.claimed ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.verifiedAbsent ? 'yes' : 'no'} |` `` (line 41). `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` has a `sanitizeCell` function (line 640, `String(text).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').replace(/\|/g, '\\|').trim()`) built for the identical purpose and already used by that file's own `renderVerifyTable` — but `sanitizeCell` is a private function, not currently in `engine-verify.js`'s `module.exports` (line 656, which lists `runVerify`, `renderVerifyTable`, `resolveArchivedRunDir`, `registerCheck`, `defaultGit`, `defaultGh`, `resolveParent`, `resolvePrNumber` — no `sanitizeCell`). An artifact string containing a literal `|` (e.g. a branch/PR-title-derived description) splits the generated row into extra columns, breaking the Step 6 report table's rendering.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add `sanitizeCell` to `engine-verify.js`'s `module.exports` (it already exists as a private function; this just makes it importable).
- [ ] In `verify-cleanup.js`, `require('../wrap-up/engine-verify')` and call `sanitizeCell(row.artifact)` before interpolating it into `renderCleanupTable`'s row string.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A test with an artifact string containing a literal `|` renders a well-formed 3-column table row (verify via `renderCleanupTable`'s output split on `|` producing exactly the expected column count for that row).
2. `engine-verify.js`'s own existing tests and usages of `sanitizeCell`/`renderVerifyTable` are unaffected by adding it to `module.exports` (a pure additive export, no signature change).

## Technical Approach
Reuse rather than duplicate: `sanitizeCell` already does exactly what's needed (pipe-escaping plus whitespace collapsing, consistent with how `renderVerifyTable` already sanitizes its own cells), so exporting it and importing it in `verify-cleanup.js` is a two-file, additive-only change — no new escaping logic to write or independently verify.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js` — `renderCleanupTable` (line 40)
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — `sanitizeCell` (line 640), `module.exports` (line 656)

## Original request
Origin: whole-branch review (e4fd2b2a8..884ed7ea, gating v6.120.0).

groups.title: /claude-tweaks:review's flow-context full-mode default isn't self-enforcing
groups.body:
Origin: reflect light from #1143
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Overview states: "When invoked by `/claude-tweaks:flow`, review runs in **full** mode by default (code + visual)." But the Input resolution section's actual mode-selection rules (1-8) are purely token-based — the literal word `full` appearing in `$ARGUMENTS` is the only thing that selects full mode. There is no rule that checks `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` (or any other flow-context signal) and defaults to full mode when no explicit mode token is present. A flow executor who invokes `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` without typing `full` explicitly silently gets **code** mode instead — no warning, no divergence from the documented default surfaced anywhere. This run (#1143's own flow continuation) hit exactly this gap: `/claude-tweaks:review #1143` was invoked without the `full` token, resolving to code mode per the skill's own Input resolution rule 1. No actual harm occurred this run (the record's `surface: backend`, so visual review would have been skipped by Step 6's own detection regardless of mode) — but on a frontend record, the same omission would silently skip the browser visual-review pass in a context where the skill's own documentation promises it always runs.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a rule to `skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Input resolution (or its own note) that defaults to full mode when `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is set (or an equivalent flow-context signal is present) and no explicit mode token (`full`/`visual`/`journey:`/`discover`) appears in `$ARGUMENTS` — making the documented "flow invokes review in full mode by default" promise self-enforcing rather than dependent on the flow executor remembering to type `full`.
- [ ] Audit `skills/flow/SKILL.md`'s own Step 4 invocation prose for the same gap — it also just says "Flow invokes `/claude-tweaks:review` in full mode by default" without specifying the mechanism that makes this true.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` invoked with `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` set and no explicit mode token resolves to full mode (verifiable by reading the updated Input resolution rule).
2. `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` invoked standalone (no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`) and no explicit mode token still resolves to code mode, unchanged — the fix must not alter standalone behavior.
3. An explicit mode token (`full`/`visual`/`journey:`/`discover`) still always wins over the flow-context default, in either context.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

groups.title: crossReferenceKeyFiles: sibling-title substring match lacks word boundaries, and re-parses/re-greps per outer unit
groups.body:
## Current State
In `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js`'s `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), sibling-title matching uses a plain lowercased substring test (`line.toLowerCase().includes(titleLower)`, line 72) with no word-boundary check — a short/generic sibling title can appear as a substring inside an unrelated longer word or phrase in another unit's Gotchas/Prerequisites text, wrongly attaching that unit's grep hits to the wrong sibling's Key Files list. Separately, `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas'/'Prerequisites')` (line 68) is recomputed inside the inner `for (const other of list)` loop on every outer `unit` iteration, even though each `other`'s section text doesn't depend on the outer unit — O(N^2) re-parsing for a decomposition batch of N sub-issues — and the injected `grep(ident)` subprocess call (line ~76) has no memoization across outer units sharing the same identifier, real avoidable subprocess-spawn cost that scales with batch size.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add a word-boundary check to the sibling-title substring match, reusing the existing `escapeRegExp` helper (`plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`) to build a `\b{escaped title}\b` regex rather than writing a new escaper — the title is user-authored text and may itself contain regex metacharacters.
- [ ] Hoist the `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas')` / `extractSection(other.body, 'Prerequisites')` computation for each `other` outside the outer `unit` loop (compute once per `other`, into a map keyed by `other`, not once per unit×other pair).
- [ ] Memoize `grep(ident)` results (a `Map<string, string[]>`) across outer units within one `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call, so the same identifier is grepped at most once per batch regardless of how many units reference it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A test with a short generic sibling title (e.g. "Fix") that also appears as a substring of an unrelated word in another unit's Gotchas text does not wrongly cross-reference.
2. A test confirms `extractSection` is called at most once per distinct `other` unit within one batch (not once per unit×other pair) — e.g. via a call-counting wrapper or spy on a batch of 3+ units.
3. A test confirms the injected `grep` is called at most once per distinct identifier within one batch, even when multiple units' Gotchas reference the same identifier.
4. All six existing tests in `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` pass unchanged.

## Technical Approach
Reuse `escapeRegExp` from `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` (already used the same way in `claim-store.js:415` to build a safe dynamic regex from untrusted text) rather than introducing a second escaping implementation. For the two performance fixes, restructure the double loop so the `other`-keyed work (section extraction) happens once per `other` before the outer `unit` loop runs, and thread a shared `Map` for grep memoization through the whole `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js` — `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), `extractSection` (line 33), the substring match (line 72), the `grep(ident)` call (line ~76)
- `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` — `escapeRegExp` (line 43), to reuse rather than reimplement
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` — 129 lines, 6 existing tests, all must stay green

## Original request
Origin: whole-branch review (e4fd2b2a8..884ed7ea, gating v6.120.0) — in #490's decomposition cross-reference feature.

groups.title: Confirm RemoteTrigger update persists notifications, then close #68's guided-creation path
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Refs #68. `skills/routine/create-and-update.md` now sets `notifications` unconditionally on the direct-create path (Step 6 body template), documents the field, and adds a Step 7 preview line stating a routine emails on every firing — all implemented and pinned by `tests/routine-notifications.test.js`. Step 8's guided-creation branch was also extended with a follow-up `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}` call, but its correctness for the `notifications` field specifically is unconfirmed: Task 0's empirical premise-check (does `RemoteTrigger update` actually persist `notifications` the same way `create` was already confirmed live) requires the `RemoteTrigger` tool, which was unavailable in both the original build session and this ledger-resolution session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` returns no match in either).

**Shaping-time fact-check (2026-08-23):** the `RemoteTrigger` tool, previously unavailable in both prior sessions, is now available in this session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` resolves it) — the same finding as sibling record #1302, filed from the same ledger-resolution pass. This shaping session did **not** attempt Task 0's actual premise-check: creating a throwaway routine via `RemoteTrigger` and confirming `notifications` persists is a real external-service mutation with no delete API to clean it up afterward (per the record's own Deliverables), which is build-time work requiring the build session's own judgment and authorization, not something to run speculatively during shaping. The build session should re-verify `RemoteTrigger` availability in its own environment before assuming this blocker is fully resolved — tool availability may be session-type-dependent (interactive vs. cloud/routine).

## Deliverables

- Re-verify `RemoteTrigger` availability via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in the build session's own environment.
- Run Task 0's premise-check: create a disabled, cron-less throwaway routine, call `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}` on it, `get` it back to confirm the value stuck, then remove the throwaway by hand at claude.ai/code/routines (no delete API exists).
- If confirmed: mark #68 AC2/AC3 met — the guided-path follow-up call in `create-and-update.md` Step 8 is already implemented and needs no further code change.
- If NOT confirmed: redesign the guided-path follow-up around whatever mechanism the probe finds actually works, and update `create-and-update.md` Step 8 accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Task 0's premise-check result (confirmed / not confirmed) is recorded in this record's resolution.
- `RemoteTrigger {action: "get"}` against a just-created routine (guided path) confirms it carries the same `notifications` value as the direct-create path — this is #68's own AC2.
- If Task 0 found the `update` mechanism does not work as assumed, `create-and-update.md` Step 8 is corrected and `tests/routine-notifications.test.js` (or a new test) pins the corrected behavior.

## Technical Approach

Re-confirm `RemoteTrigger` availability first (tool access may differ from this shaping session's environment). With the tool available, create a disabled, cron-less throwaway routine via the guided-creation path, call `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}`, then `RemoteTrigger {action: "get"}` to confirm the value persisted — matching the same confirmation already done for the direct-create path. Clean up the throwaway routine manually at claude.ai/code/routines afterward (no delete API exists — do not leave it dangling).
